correctness.rationale: With the counting norm and the stated unitary DFT, modulation at a maximizing frequency and rescaling reduce the quotient to minimization at Fourier value 1 at zero (source mass q). Strict convexity and the independent coordinate dilations and swap force the unique constrained optimizer onto the two support orbits, also for q=2; orthogonality works for any nontrivial additive character and every prime power. If r=q−1, the three Fourier classes have values 1,U,V with 2U−V=1 and multiplicities 1,2r,r². Weighted Hölder gives 1≤(2r|U|⁴+r²|V|⁴)^(1/4)(2r^(−1/3)+r^(−2/3))^(3/4); equality at U=r^(1/3)/(1+2r^(1/3)), V=−1/(1+2r^(1/3)) proves the minimum and fixes phases. Both magnitudes are below 1, so this constrained optimizer attains the original quotient. Inverting the two-level transform gives precisely the mass-q seed, and undoing the normalization gives all modulated and scaled optimizers. The central numerator 2+2(q−1)^(1/3)−q decreases for real q≥2 and changes sign between 5 and 6; 6 is not a prime power. The nonconstant norm term is asymptotic to q/8. The supplied artifacts/check_certificate.py was inspected (character transforms and finite perturbations only) and not run; it is not needed for the exact proof.
